newsitem.title: USA: Perot voters seen giving Clinton 'back door' win.
newsitem.headline: Perot voters seen giving Clinton 'back door' win.

text.p: Republican National Committee Chairman Haley Barbour urged Ross Perot supporters Friday to vote for Bob Dole in order to avert another "back-door" victory by President Clinton.

"A vote for Perot amounts to a vote for Clinton," Barbour told Southern reporters in a conference call. "Clinton slipped in the back door of the White House the first time with only 43 percent of the vote," Barbour said.
"People who voted for Perot in 1992 don't want Clinton to slip back in the back door of the White House."
Barbour said there was no way the Reform Party presidential candidate could win the Nov. 5 election but his supporters could hurt Dole by sticking with Perot.

"There's never been any question in the last six to eight months of 1996 but that either Bill Clinton or Bob Dole's going to be the next president of the United States," he said. "Clinton's best hope for re-election is to split the vote of the opposition -- a vote for Perot which splits the opposition."
On Thursday, Perot ridiculed Dole's plea that he quit the presidential race and back Dole as "weird and totally inconsequential." The Texas billionaire said he was in the race to stay.

Barbour also predicted the Republican Party would improve on the gains it made in the 1994 congressional elections in the South, where a majority of senators, representatives and governors are now Republicans.

"I anticipate we will see Republican majorities in additional state legislatures in the South this year," he said. "The realignment in the South that has been going on a considerable amunt of time has been a rolling realignment and it continues to be on a roll for Republicans."
